title: David Spares Saul in the Cave
text:
King Saul, jealous of the young warrior David, was hunting him to kill him. With three thousand chosen men, Saul pursued David into the wild country around En Gedi, near the Dead Sea. On the way, Saul went alone into a cave to relieve himself. He did not know that David and his men were hiding deep in the same cave.

David's men whispered that this was the day God had promised: his enemy had been delivered into his hand. David crept forward and quietly cut off the corner of Saul's robe. Even that troubled his conscience. He told his men that God forbid he should lift his hand against the Lord's anointed, and he would not let them attack Saul.

Saul left the cave and went on his way. David came out after him and called: "My lord the king!" When Saul looked back, David bowed to the ground and held up the piece of the robe. Today, he said, you have seen that the Lord put you into my hand in the cave, and I would not harm you. Let the Lord judge between us.

Saul wept aloud. "Is that your voice, my son David?" he said. "You are more righteous than I. You have repaid me with good, while I have repaid you with evil." Saul went home, and David and his men went back up to their stronghold.
lesson: Having the power to strike a rival is not the same as having the right. Restraint at that moment shows others what kind of leader you will be, and can disarm an enemy better than force.
location: En Gedi, near the Dead Sea (modern Israel)
